decisions.question: Should the first formal model use the smallest aggregate plus a separate bounded broker refinement, or include a bounded broker directly?
decisions.why_consequential: Determines where queue, relaunch, RESET, consultation and update/Stop obligations are proved before model freeze.

options.label: Small aggregate plus explicit broker refinement
options.tradeoff: Keeps canonical state space small; every broker assumption must have bounded executable traces and a refinement mapping.

options.label: Bounded broker inside first model
options.tradeoff: Exposes cross-boundary races in one model; increases state space and abstraction work.

decisions.reason: Preserves existing M1 obligations while testing concrete process and protocol counterexamples at an explicit boundary. Move a broker event into the model if its refinement cannot be stated or falsified independently.
decisions.fixture_implications: Bounded traces must cover process ownership, consultation, queue saturation, reset/replay, relaunch and configuration/update/Stop ordering while retaining the six M1 obligations.
decisions.dependency: Small source-informed interface probes and explicit mapping of the six immutable M1 obligations.
decisions.falsifier: A necessary broker obligation cannot be expressed or independently checked as a refinement, or an interleaving violates the aggregate obligations; move that state into the first model.

decisions.question: Which persistent-assistant decision classes may amend GoalSpec, beyond choices already permitted inside existing grants?
decisions.why_consequential: Configurable assistant rights are accepted, but current GoalSpec amendments remain Owner-only; changing that boundary requires a separately bounded constitutional/M1 proposal.

options.label: Retain Owner-only GoalSpec amendments
options.tradeoff: Assistants can consult and make already-granted routine choices; strategic scope changes still wait for Owner.

options.label: Propose an explicit delegated amendment whitelist
options.tradeoff: May reduce Owner interruptions, but requires exact classes, ceilings, receipts, revocation tests and a separately authorized contract amendment.

decisions.reason: Meets persistent identity and configurable routine rights without silently changing immutable contracts. Use consultation evidence to identify any specific amendment class worth delegating later.
decisions.fixture_implications: An attempted consultant or expired lease amendment must stay rejected under current contracts; any accepted whitelist needs separate red/green authority and revocation fixtures.
decisions.dependency: Current Owner-only GoalSpec amendment rule; granting routine decision rights does not grant amendment rights.
decisions.falsifier: A representative authorized routine workflow requires an amendment and cannot complete through ordinary delegated decisions without repeated Owner intervention; then test an explicit bounded whitelist proposal.

not_owner_questions: All ten questionnaire answers and the seven critical names remain accepted.
Personal inventory is intentionally unspecified; future run packets supply actual authorized resources.
Language, store, framework, numerical presets and recovery compatibility windows remain research comparisons.
Eligibility or missing-control evidence must become a concrete release tradeoff before requesting any scope reduction. No reduction is proposed or approved here.
